purpose: Measure whether zero observed night assignments means zero employer night demand, without activating an unsafe or unaccepted shift path.
source: Authenticated Gmail read-back of weekly shift-submission receipts; no message identifiers, account identifiers, names, locations, or secrets are stored.

observed_categories: specific weekdays had many night vacancies

correction.previous_inference: No night assignment notices were found, so employer night inventory was treated as unobserved.
correction.corrected_inference: Zero night assignments cannot be used as evidence of zero employer demand because the user selected zero night shifts across all 38 parsed weekly receipts while the employer repeatedly signaled night demand.
correction.what_is_now_verified: Historical night demand exists and was repeatedly solicited.
what_remains_unverified: whether the current form offers a safe suitable night

decision.reason: Historical supply evidence improves feasibility but is not a current accepted assignment. Safety and current inventory remain unresolved.
safe_activation_gate: the current normal weekly form itself presents a suitable night option or explicit current demand
the user personally confirms physical safety and willingness
no day-night consecutive work or unsafe recovery pattern
decision.next_trigger: A current shift-form receipt, assignment notice, or non-sensitive user completion signal that includes an accepted night shift.

success_condition: At least one current safe night shift is personally selected, accepted by the employer, completed, and countable at the verified contract rate.
withdrawal_condition: No current safe night option appears, safe return is unavailable, the employer does not accept it, or the user does not choose it.
privacy: No employer name, person name, address, email, staff number, message identifier, account identifier, location, coworker, or secret is stored.
